title: The AI automation architect
oneliner: The automation architect works across all business units and architecture domains to find where business, data, application, and technology automation pay off - then infuses AI into the automation framework.
says: An automation architect works with business, data, technology, and application architects across all lines of business to find where business automation, data automation, and application and technology automation can be implemented; prioritizes and implements the high-value use cases; and infuses AI into the automation framework so the organization gets more benefit from AI and automation together.
explained: This is the most enterprise-shaped role in his catalog: horizontal by design. Where the solution architect owns one system, the automation architect owns the portfolio of automation opportunities - which means the real skills are discovery (where does manual work concentrate?), prioritization (which automations pay back fastest?), and coalition (every automation crosses someone's team).

The AI-infusion point marks the difference from the RPA era. Classic automation moves data between screens on fixed rules; AI-infused automation reads documents, interprets requests, and handles exceptions - the trend from his RPA-to-agents reel given a job title. For architects looking for a seat that touches everything, this is it.
takeaway: Automation architecture is a portfolio job: find the manual work, rank by payback, and make AI the layer that handles judgment, not just keystrokes.
